children: Brazil's lower house of Congress late on Monday approved a government-backed fiscal package aimed at shoring up public finances, though investors view the measures as insufficient to address the country's deteriorating debt outlook.

The package will allow additional budget freezes to help meet fiscal targets, effectively capping annual spending growth at 2%, while also cutting tax breaks and restricting the use of tax credits to boost revenue when fiscal goals are at risk.
The bill, which had already been approved by the Senate last week, is expected to improve public finances by up to 60 billion reais ($10.02 billion) in 2027
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will now sign it into law
Lula's economic team sees the fiscal package as critical to achieving next year's primary surplus target of 0.5% of gross domestic product
Brazil's gross debt has risen by more than 11 percentage points since Lula took office in 2023, reaching 82.9% of GDP
The Brazilian currency has weakened about 19% since the leftist leader's reelection in late October, amid concerns that he may not implement reforms investors deem necessary to stabilize debt
Government officials have said the bill is just a first step and more measures will follow
